notes: Built from the PDF only (02-20000-60, Reviewed 04/23/26, Revised 05/15/26). The download holds a single clean copy; there is no redline. effective_date is the printed Revised date of this version (the Original Effective Date 10/15/16 is the first version); reviewed_date is the printed Reviewed date.

TKA list structure (hardest call): 'one or more of the following criteria are met' is a list of six single-bullet indications joined by OR, followed by a seventh compound indication 'Advanced joint disease ... AND Pain or functional disability ... AND Failure of at least 3 months of conservative non-surgical management'. The AND connectors attach Pain/disability and the conservative-management trial to the advanced-joint-disease alternative only, not to the fracture, malignancy, osteotomy-failure, failed-UKA or AVN alternatives (a distal femur fracture cannot sensibly require 3 months of conservative care). A reviewer could read Pain and Conservative management as applying to every alternative; we did not, and the tree is any(6 single indications, all(advanced disease, pain/disability, conservative trial)).

The bullet 'There are no contraindications* to total knee arthroplasty for any indication above' carries no connector but 'for any indication above' makes it a general requirement for every TKA alternative; modelled as not(any(the four starred contraindications)) inside the TKA pathway's all. The same bullet under Revision arthroplasty is modelled the same way. The sentence itself is not a criterion; the four contraindication items are.

The starred list '*Contraindications for total and revision knee arthroplasty' (bacteremia, active skin infection/open wound at the site, neuropathic arthritis, rapidly progressive neurological disease) is shared by the TKA and Revision pathways; the same criterion ids are reused. 'Active systemic bacteremia', 'Active skin infection or open wound within the planned surgical site of the knee' and 'Rapidly progressive neurological disease' also appear verbatim in the UKA contraindication list and reuse the same ids; 'Neuropathic arthritis' (TKA/revision) and 'Inflammatory or neuropathic arthritis' (UKA) are different requirements and separate criteria.

Conservative management for TKA: the criterion is the 3-month documented trial (duration_months >= 3) and the eight modalities are an any() beneath it ('includes 1 or more of the following'). Modalities are each their own criterion so a chart can show which one was tried. 'as is reasonable' / 'as appropriate' qualifiers are kept in the text; they are not modelled as waivers because the modalities are already alternatives.

Conservative management for UKA: 'includes all of the following' is an all() of the modalities. The two '(unless contraindicated)' waivers are modelled as any(modality tried, modality contraindicated) at the requirement. The two waiver criteria have the identical verbatim text 'unless contraindicated' (the PDF's exact words at both bullets) and are told apart by id and question. The PDF reads 'Failure of at least of 3 months' (sic); the text is copied with the typo.

UKA: 'None of the following contraindications for unicompartmental arthroplasty are present' is indented in the PDF as the last sub-bullet of the conservative-management list. We placed it at the pathway's top level as not(any(10 contraindications)) because it is a contraindication screen, not a component of conservative management; all(all(a,b),c) and all(a,b,c) evaluate identically so no logic is changed by that placement.

UKA 'No anterior cruciate ligament instability' is modelled as not(leaf 'anterior cruciate ligament instability') so a chart stating the ACL is intact (NOT_MET on instability) satisfies it and a silent chart stays INSUFFICIENT; the leaf text is the verbatim substring.

UKA Kellgren-Lawrence 'Grade 3 or 4' is a number threshold >= 3 (the grading scale 0-4 is printed under the position statement; the scale itself is a definition, not a requirement, and is not in the tree). 'Total arc of motion by goniometer > 90 degrees' is number > 90 degrees. 'Flexion contracture > 15 degrees', 'Varus deformity > 15 degrees', 'Valgus deformity > 20 degrees' are number thresholds on contraindication criteria.

The varus (medial UKA) and valgus (lateral UKA) contraindications are compartment-specific but 27446 covers either compartment; both stay in the UKA not(any()) and each question states which compartment it applies to. A reviewer could instead split medial and lateral UKA into two pathways.

Bullets that list alternatives with 'or' inside an OR list ('Periprosthetic fracture or aseptic loosening', 'Fracture or dislocation of the patella', 'Disabling pain or functional disability', 'Dislocation of the knee joint'/'Instability of the knee joint' kept separate as printed) are kept as one criterion per bullet, since splitting them inside an any() changes nothing. 'Crepitus, effusion, or swelling with limited range of motion' is one criterion; whether 'with limited range of motion' attaches to all three findings or only to swelling is ambiguous and left to the question.

TKA 'Advanced joint disease demonstrated by radiographic or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) evidence of subchondral cysts, ... avascular necrosis)' is copied with the PDF's stray closing parenthesis. The list of imaging findings is read as any one finding sufficing; 'avascular necrosis' appears both here and as its own indication 'Avascular necrosis of the knee'.

Code-to-pathway mapping: the coding table does not tie codes to sections. 27447 (medial AND lateral compartments, total knee arthroplasty) -> Total knee arthroplasty; 27486 and 27487 (revision of total knee arthroplasty) -> Revision arthroplasty; 27446 (medial OR lateral compartment) -> Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty; 27438 (arthroplasty, patella; with prosthesis) -> Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty because the UKA criterion names the patellofemoral compartment as a single compartment. Conversion of a failed UKA to a TKA is billed 27447 and is covered by the TKA indication 'Failure of previous unicompartmental knee replacement'. All five codes are covered; the document names no non-covered or investigational code and has no exclusion statements.

Program exceptions: FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines; Medicare Advantage products: the LCD Major Joint Replacement (Hip and Knee) L33618 'was reviewed on the last guideline review date', which we read (as the hand-built varicose vein fixture does) as Medicare Advantage following the LCD rather than this guideline. The step-therapy protocol exemption paragraph (Florida law 627.42393) is a process note, not a requirement, and is not in the tree.

Left out of the tree: the DESCRIPTION section (UpToDate summaries, including their list of TKA contraindications and the historical UKA candidate profile such as age > 60, weight < 82 kg, deformity < 15 degrees) because it is background evidence, not the position statement; the Kellgren-Lawrence grading definitions; the guideline update history.
